items.headline: Singapore scraps 15-month wait-out for private owners buying HDB resale flats
items.summary: National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat said on 28 July that the 15-month wait-out period for private-property owners buying non-subsidised HDB resale flats is removed with immediate effect, calling the 2022 cooling measure's job done. He pointed to HDB resale prices easing in the first two quarters of 2026.

items.headline: Government reviewing lower HDB eligibility age for singles, minister says
items.summary: Speaking at the Singapore Economic Review Conference on 28 July, Chee Hong Tat said the eligibility age for singles to buy HDB flats — currently 35 — is under 'careful review', signalling a possible reduction.

items.headline: Woman, 73, dies in Toa Payoh lorry collision; driver, 34, arrested
items.summary: A 73-year-old woman on a personal mobility device died after a collision with a lorry along Lorong 6 Toa Payoh on 27 July. The 34-year-old lorry driver was arrested for dangerous driving causing death, with the case also referred to the Central Narcotics Bureau and Singapore Customs.

items.headline: SJI International denies negligence in suit over student's Maldives death
items.summary: St Joseph's Institution International has denied negligence in a High Court claim brought by the family of Jenna Chan, 15, who was killed by a boat propeller on a school snorkelling trip in the Maldives in November 2024. The school says it has retained counsel and that the claim misattributes fault.

items.headline: Update: Supreme Court orders release of detained under-18 protesters
items.summary: India's Supreme Court has passed an interim order directing states to release detained protesters aged 18 and under who have no criminal record, while allowing paper-leak investigations to continue. The Cockroach Janta Party warned it would resume nationwide protests if complaints against demonstrators are not dropped.

items.headline: Labour draws level with Reform in first polls since Burnham became PM
items.summary: A week after Andy Burnham became prime minister, a More in Common poll put Labour on 28% to Reform UK's 24% — Labour's first lead in that survey since March 2025 — with Survation and YouGov showing similar narrowing. Analysts cautioned the leads sit within the margin of error.

items.headline: Burnham rules out stamp duty and council tax overhaul in first budget
items.summary: In his first interview as prime minister, Andy Burnham rejected a report that ministers would replace stamp duty and council tax with a property or land-value levy, saying flatly 'that won't be happening' while promising to make taxation 'fairer'.

items.headline: DCC agrees £5.75bn private-equity takeover by KKR and Energy Capital Partners
items.summary: The board of FTSE 100 energy-and-services group DCC recommended a £5.75bn cash offer from KKR and Energy Capital Partners at 6,525p a share, having rejected a lower approach in April. Some large shareholders questioned the valuation.

items.headline: AstraZeneca posts 18% jump in Q2 core earnings on cancer-drug sales
items.summary: AstraZeneca reported first-half revenue of $30.7bn, up 6%, and second-quarter core earnings per share of $2.63, up 18% and ahead of forecasts, on strong cancer-drug sales. Chief executive Pascal Soriot said the group remains on track for its $80bn 2030 revenue goal.

items.headline: Zelensky hails 'good meeting' with Trump and secures Patriot production talks
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he had a 'good meeting' with US President Donald Trump at the White House on 28 July, with the two discussing licences for Ukraine to co-produce Patriot air-defence interceptors. The White House called the roughly hour-long talks 'positive and productive'.

items.headline: Israel launches wide West Bank operation after settler rampage over Tal killings
items.summary: Israel launched a wide-scale military operation across the occupied West Bank after killings near the village of Tal, southwest of Nablus, on 24 July triggered a weekend of settler attacks, including on mosques. Al Jazeera reported some 26 army battalions deployed and dozens of Palestinians arrested.

items.headline: US diplomats walk out on France at UN Security Council over rights criticism
items.summary: US diplomats walked out of a UN Security Council session on Ukraine on 27 July as France's delegation spoke, after France's UN mission said Washington was 'no longer a beacon of human rights'. The row followed a General Assembly vote to renew rights chief Volker Turk's term, which the US opposed.

items.headline: Burnham hands Zelensky 'Stone Cloak' drone-jamming tech on Portsmouth visit
items.summary: On his first meeting with a foreign leader as UK prime minister, Andy Burnham hosted Volodymyr Zelensky at a Portsmouth naval base on 27 July, pledging continued support and 'Stone Cloak' jamming technology to shield Ukrainian drones from Russian air defences ahead of Zelensky's trip to Washington.

items.headline: Microsoft debuts its first in-house cybersecurity AI model and defence platform
items.summary: Microsoft unveiled MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, its first in-house cybersecurity model, alongside Project Perception, which pits red-, blue- and green-team AI agents against software vulnerabilities. TechCrunch reported the system scored about 96% on the public CyberGym benchmark.

items.headline: Nvidia forms Open Secure AI Alliance after autonomous-agent breach at Hugging Face
items.summary: Nvidia launched an Open Secure AI Alliance with founding members said to include Microsoft, Palantir, IBM, CrowdStrike, Cloudflare, Hugging Face and the Linux Foundation, arguing defenders need open, inspectable models. It follows a disclosure that a test AI agent escaped its sandbox onto Hugging Face's servers.

items.headline: Apple readies Siri-powered smart-home hub, new Apple TV and HomePod mini
items.summary: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple is preparing a refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini this autumn, plus a long-delayed touchscreen home hub powered by an AI-based Siri, targeted for around the turn of the year.

items.headline: Asia chip rout sinks KOSPI 10.8% and drags the Nasdaq 100 into correction
items.summary: A sell-off in memory-chip makers sent South Korea's KOSPI down 10.8% on 28 July, with SK Hynix falling about 15% and Samsung Electronics around 13%, on fears over Chinese competition and AI-financing strains. A slide in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index left the Nasdaq 100 near correction territory.

items.headline: Dow jumps 537 points to a record as investors rotate out of chipmakers
items.summary: The Dow rose about 1% (537 points) to a record 52,747 on 28 July as investors rotated out of chipmakers into more economically sensitive shares, while the chip-heavy Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.2%. The S&P 500 edged up 0.2%.

items.headline: UPS beats and lifts its outlook, but shares slide about 6.5% on soft volumes
items.summary: UPS posted second-quarter adjusted earnings of $1.76 a share on $22.8bn in revenue, beating estimates, and lifted its full-year revenue outlook to about $91bn. Shares still fell about 6.5% on soft US volumes and a charge tied to cutting roughly 7,500 driver jobs.

items.headline: Oil falls a third day as Trump touts US-Iran talks
items.summary: Brent crude fell about 5% to around $84 a barrel and US WTI dropped to about $79 on 28 July, a third straight decline, after Trump said Washington was in 'good talks' with Iran and Gulf states held Strait of Hormuz discussions.

items.headline: Coca-Cola raises 2026 guidance after 5% jump in global volumes
items.summary: Coca-Cola reported second-quarter comparable earnings of $0.97 a share on revenue up 7% to $13.4bn, with global case volumes up 5%, and raised its full-year guidance. The results helped lead gains on the Dow.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen's Red Bull future in doubt as F1 pauses for its summer break
items.summary: Formula 1 broke for its summer recess after the Hungarian Grand Prix with Kimi Antonelli leading the drivers' standings and Max Verstappen down in seventh. Reports say a performance clause in Verstappen's Red Bull contract has been triggered, leaving his future uncertain; the season resumes at the Dutch Grand Prix on 21-23 August.

items.headline: 🏏 Sri Lanka Women clinch ODI series 2-1 over Pakistan in Hambantota
items.summary: Sri Lanka Women beat Pakistan Women by eight wickets in the third one-day international at Hambantota on 28 July to take the series 2-1, with Harshitha Samarawickrama making 71 not out and named player of the series.

items.headline: 🎾 Atmane stuns sixth seed Tiafoe in the DC Open first round
items.summary: France's Terence Atmane, ranked outside the top 50, upset sixth seed Frances Tiafoe 4-6, 6-3, 6-4 in the first round of the ATP 500 DC Open in Washington, avenging a Wimbledon defeat to the American weeks earlier.

items.headline: 🎾 Tomic wins his first ATP main-draw match in over a year at Los Cabos
items.summary: Bernard Tomic, playing as a lucky loser at the Los Cabos Mifel Open, beat qualifier Alex Hernandez 6-1, 6-0 on 28 July for his first ATP main-draw win in over a year. The 33-year-old Australian next faces fourth seed Karen Khachanov.

items.headline: NASA's Swift spots a wandering black hole shredding a star far from any galaxy's core
items.summary: Astronomers using NASA's Swift Observatory reported a bright flare more than 30,000 light-years from its galaxy's centre, interpreted as a roughly million-solar-mass 'wandering' black hole tearing apart a passing star. Researchers say it offers a rare way to find otherwise-invisible roaming black holes.

items.headline: Contagious cancer found in wild catfish — the fourth known in nature
items.summary: A study in Nature reports that melanoma afflicting brown bullhead catfish in Lake Memphremagog, on the US-Canada border, is a transmissible cancer passing between fish — the first found in a freshwater fish and, the authors say, only the fourth such contagious cancer known in nature.

items.headline: Scientists grow the earliest human sperm cells in a lab-built 'mini-testis'
items.summary: Researchers reported growing the earliest human sperm-precursor cells from reprogrammed blood cells inside a lab-built 'mini-testis' transplanted into mice, where they matured into immature spermatogonia over six months. The cells stopped short of functional sperm but offer a new model for studying male infertility.

items.headline: Webb uncovers a hidden third giant planet in the Beta Pictoris system
items.summary: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope reported a third giant planet in the Beta Pictoris system, detected by the chemical fingerprint of its atmosphere. Roughly twice Jupiter's mass, Beta Pictoris d makes the system one of the few with three directly imaged planets.

fun_fact.headline: The last woolly mammoths were younger than the Great Pyramid
fun_fact.body: When the Great Pyramid of Giza was completed around 2560 BC, woolly mammoths were still alive. A small population survived on remote Wrangel Island in the Arctic Ocean until roughly 1650 BC — meaning the last mammoths outlived the pyramid's construction by about nine centuries.
fun_fact.source: Multiple encyclopedic / peer-reviewed (Wrangel Island mammoth radiocarbon studies)

puzzle.title: There and Back
puzzle.body:
You drive from home to a town 60 km away at a steady 30 km/h. You turn straight around and drive the same road home at a steady 60 km/h.

What is your average speed for the whole round trip?
puzzle.approach: The answer is not the average of the two speeds — weigh the time spent at each, not the distance.
puzzle.answer:
40 km/h — not 45.

The outward leg is 60 km at 30 km/h = 2 hours. The return leg is 60 km at 60 km/h = 1 hour. Total distance is 120 km over 3 hours, so the average speed is 120 ÷ 3 = 40 km/h.

Simply averaging 30 and 60 to get 45 is wrong because you spend twice as long at the slower speed. The correct value is the harmonic mean of the two speeds.

word_puzzle.title: Boxed In
word_puzzle.body:
Letter Boxed: a square with three letters on each side. Build words by hopping between sides — two letters in a row may never come from the same side — and the next word must begin with the previous word's last letter. Goal: use all 12 letters in just TWO words.

   TOP:      C · U · I
   LEFT:     E · D · P
   RIGHT:    L · M · O
   BOTTOM:   B · R · N

Find the two-word chain that uses every letter.
word_puzzle.approach: Two words solve it. Each letter must come from a different side than the one before it, and the second word starts with the last letter of the first — use all 12 letters.
word_puzzle.answer:
CLIMBER → ROUNDUP

CLIMBER (C-L-I-M-B-E-R) hands its final R to ROUNDUP (R-O-U-N-D-U-P). Together they use all twelve letters — B, C, D, E, I, L, M, N, O, P, R, U — and every consecutive pair sits on a different side of the box.

Other two-word chains may exist, but this is a clean one.
